quote: I I'm wondering how in the heck you could put solar array up there, but go ahead with as long as you know that.
stewart_read: Customer surfaces a self-disqualifying concern unprompted; this is a legitimacy/trust moment the rep must resolve before anything else can proceed.
coaching_implication: Reinforce that opening objections like this should be answered with specificity, not just reassurance, since specificity reduces suspicion per protocols.how_did_you_get_my_number logic.

quote: Honestly, your roof your roof is fine. And how it is, it's totally fine. The the thing they'll probably care about more is the trees.
stewart_read: Rep answers confidently but with no actual technical grounding for why east/west orientation is fine — a plausible-sounding claim without content, which works here but is a coachable risk if a sharper customer pushed back.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could genuinely know east/west roofs work fine for solar and this is accurate knowledge, not a gap — the schema doesn't have data to confirm either way.
coaching_implication: Confirm with the rep what he actually knows about roof orientation vs. what he's guessing; if guessing, redirect to the specialist escape hatch instead of asserting confidently.

quote: So Roughly, I know you can't give me a specific.
stewart_read: Customer is explicitly asking about government help / savings amount tied to his motivation to 'do the right thing' and save money — a natural anchor point. The rep answers with the bill-swap program mechanic but never ties it back to the customer's own stated motivations or bill pain.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be intentionally deferring numbers to the closer per numeric_discipline, which is correct scope discipline, not a miss.
coaching_implication: The program-mechanic answer itself is fine and appropriately vague on numbers, but the rep should have asked for the bill dollar amount here and used it as the emotional anchor rather than moving straight to qualifying questions.

quote: my interest is also to do the right thing.
stewart_read: Customer gives a values-based motivation (environmental/ethical) beyond bill savings. The rep acknowledges it in one line and never returns to it later in the pitch, appointment framing, or close — the anchor is captured but never reused.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the customer's age and hearing difficulty, the rep may have been triaging for basic comprehension over rhetorical reinforcement — a reasonable call-management tradeoff, though it still leaves the anchor unused.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close the loop on stated motivations by name at the appointment set or in the follow-up text — e.g., referencing 'doing the right thing' when confirming tomorrow's appointment.

quote: I don't know offhand because we do it automatically.
stewart_read: No bill dollar figure was ever captured — the rep supplied a placeholder range himself rather than the customer stating a number.
coaching_implication: When the customer can't recall the bill amount, the rep should ask about pulling it from the bill/kWh history later in the same conversation rather than filling in a guessed range and moving on — the guessed number gives nothing to anchor emotionally.

quote: We could just talk. You into football?
stewart_read: With the son occupied, the rep fills dead air with small talk that keeps the customer engaged and prevents a cold hang-up during a multi-minute wait — a reasonable rapport move for this specific stall, not a tempo/pitch energy-match issue.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as wasted time, but the customer responds warmly (bike racing story) and stays on the line through a long technical delay, suggesting it served its purpose.
coaching_implication: This is a fine instinct to reinforce — filling dead air during waits keeps the customer present — but the rep should keep an eye on the clock so small talk doesn't substitute for the button-up steps later.

stewart_read: The rep initiated a text-based photo request without first confirming the phone could receive texts, and only discovered the landline issue after several minutes invested in that path.
coaching_implication: Ask 'is this a cell phone or landline' before proposing to text anything — a 10-second check that would have avoided the mid-call pivot to email.

quote: We got you down. We'll see you tomorrow at at 10AM. Okay? 10AM.
stewart_read: A date and time are locked, but none of Ion's button-up scaffolding is present: no one-hour block statement, no no-driving/computer instruction, no verbal 'is that fair?' handshake, and no on-call promise of a confirmation text.
coaching_implication: This is the single highest-leverage fix for this rep on this call — the button-up sequence is a scripted, low-effort add that materially affects show rate, and it was skipped almost entirely despite a clean close on date/time.
